newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS BLANK AVALANCHE IN BATTLE OF CONFERENCE LEADERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS BLANK AVALANCHE IN BATTLE OF CONFERENCE LEADERS.

text.p: Ron Hextall made 19 saves for his fifth shutout of the season as the Philadelphia Flyers blanked Colorado 2-0 to keep the Avalanche from cracking the 100-point plateau on Sunday.
Pat Falloon and Joel Otto scored for the Flyers in a showdown of conference leaders and a potential preview of the Stanley Cup Finals.

Hextall made eight saves in each of the first two periods and faced only three shots in the third for his 19th career shutout as Philadelphia moved two points ahead of New Jersey for the lead in the Eastern Conference.
The defending Stanley Cup champion Avalanche had their four-game winning streak halted but still hold a five-point edge over Dallas for the top spot in the West.
"It was a wonderful job tonight there was a lot of passion," Philadelphia coach Terry Murray said.
"All the battles you have to win to play well, the one-on-one stuff, the grinding, the second efforts, it was all evident tonight. This was a team win."
The Flyers won despite missing star centre Eric Lindros from the lineup after he suffered a bruised lower right calf in Saturday's tie with the Islanders.
Falloon gave the Flyers a 1-0 lead at 7:22 of the first period, snapping a wrist shot through goaltender Patrick Roy's pads off a 2-on-1 with Paul Coffey.
With 7:51 left in the third period, Otto added an insurance tally. John LeClair had the puck behind the net and flipped it in front and Otto jammed it past Roy.
"It's not hard to explain what happened tonight, they simply outplayed us," said Roy, who made 29 saves.
In St Louis, Jere Lehtinen scored twice in the third period and Mike Modano added a goal and two assists as the Dallas Stars beat the Blues 4-1.
Arturs Irbe made 21 saves and Dave Reid added his 17th goal for Dallas, which improved to 6-0-2 in a season-high eight game unbeaten streak.
Modano and Lehtinen each had short-handed goals as Dallas went 0-for-5 with the man advantage but scored twice on St Louis powerplays.
Robert Petrovicky scored the lone goal for St Louis at 8:31 of the second period, but Dallas responded with four unanswered goals.
In Chicago, Jim Cummins and Eric Daze scored 14 seconds apart in a four-goal first period as the Blackhawks skated to a 5-3 win over the Detroit Red Wings.
Sergei Krivokrasov added a pair of goals for the Blackhawks, each time restoring a three-goal Chicago lead.
Chicago scored on three of its first four shots, forcing the removal of Red Wings goaltender Mike Vernon, who was replaced by Kevin Hodson just 7:19 into the contest.
The win moved Chicago into a tie with Calgary for the eighth and final playoff spot in the the West.
Brendan Shanahan notched his 45th goal for Detroit and set up a goal by Steve Yzerman.
In Edmonton, Paul Kariya had a goal and two assists and Mikhail Shtalenkov made 32 saves in relief of Guy Hebert as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim defeated the Oilers 4-1.
Hebert stopped all 10 shots he faced in the first period but suffered dehydration and did not start the second period.

Teemu Selanne picked up his 47th goal -- tying him with Philadelphia's John LeClair for the league lead -- and added an assist Kariya's powerplay tally in the first period before leaving the game in the second with a strained oblique muscle.
Jari Kurri added two assist for Anaheim.
Andrei Kovalenko scored his team-leading 30th goal for the Oilers in the final minute of the second period.
